title: Staff member reported a newsletter as suspicious

verdict.executive_summary: A low-severity user-reported phish alert fired because Maryam Iqbal used the Report Phishing button on a newsletter from newsletter@marketwatchdaily.example at 2026-08-29T08:31:00Z. Available evidence indicates this was a legitimate subscribed marketing email sent from a long-established benign sender to 62 internal recipients, with no attachment, a clean marketing URL, and no clicks or replies. This matters only as a user-report event; there is no evidence of malicious email activity or user impact.
verdict.rationale: Playbook coverage exists for user-reported phishing. The detection itself only claims that a user reported an email, not that phishing occurred. Required checks were completed: sender history shows three years of incident-free mail; all sender-authentication checks passed; the domain is consistently benign across all configured TI feeds; the message had no attachment and only one normal marketing URL; the same newsletter was delivered to 62 recipients as a normal subscription; mail logs confirm nobody clicked or replied; and the same sender has been reported six times before with harmless outcomes and no later misclassification. The specific innocent explanation is that Maryam Iqbal did not recognise the sender name and reported a legitimate subscribed newsletter, which is directly supported by the user statement and the mail characteristics. The deciding fact is whether the reported message was in fact a legitimate subscription newsletter rather than a phishing lure; that fact was obtained from sender history, authentication results, recipient pattern, content, and prior identical harmless cases, and it supports the innocent explanation. No hard trigger applies, no watchlist or crown-jewel context is present, all enrichment sources answered, and the alert meets the Wave 1 close condition for marketing mail with clean URL/no attachment and no clicks or replies. This is therefore a Close as False Positive: the rule correctly detected a report action, but the reported email is not malicious and not what a phishing investigation needs escalated for.
verdict.claim_restated: A staff member reported an email as suspicious using the phishing-report button.
clean_findings: Sender newsletter@marketwatchdaily.example has emailed the company for three years without incident.
All sender-identity checks passed, indicating the email was genuinely sent from marketwatchdaily.example.
The only URL, https://marketwatchdaily.example/reports/q3-benchmark, was described as a normal marketing page with nothing to fill in.
The same newsletter was delivered to 62 internal recipients as a normal subscription.
Mail logs confirm nobody clicked the link.
Mail logs confirm nobody replied to the message.
Threat intelligence from Feed A, Feed B, and Feed C all rate marketwatchdaily.example as benign.
Historical dispositions show six prior reports of this exact sender/pattern, all closed as harmless and none later found misclassified.
Behavioural baseline comparison found no deviations on any measured dimension.
User m.iqbal@northbank.example is a standard user with low sign-in risk and normal managed device usage.
Host NB-RES-045 is low criticality, not internet-exposed, fully patched, and has healthy EDR.
No related alerts were found in the correlation window.
verdict.innocent_explanation: Maryam Iqbal received a legitimate subscribed newsletter from MarketWatch Daily, did not recognise the sender name, and reported it out of caution. Evidence: the sender has a three-year benign history with the company, sender-authentication checks passed, the content is consistent with a subscription newsletter, the domain is benign across all TI feeds, 62 employees received the same message as a normal subscription, there was no attachment, the URL was a normal marketing page with no credential collection, nobody clicked or replied, and the reporter explicitly said they simply did not recognise the sender's name.
verdict.malicious_explanation: An attacker could have used a legitimate-looking external newsletter domain and benign marketing-style content as a lure to build trust or stage later phishing, relying on the fact that the message appears routine. This would be supported by spoofed sender indicators, malicious or credential-harvesting landing content, unusual targeting, clicks or replies, related alerts, or evidence that the sender/domain had recently changed behaviour or reputation.
verdict.deciding_fact: Whether the reported email was a legitimate subscription newsletter from the established sender, rather than a phishing lure.
verdict.containment_considered: No containment was taken. Quarantine, URL blocking, or account actions were considered unnecessary because the message was authenticated, benign in context, had no attachment, the URL was assessed as a normal marketing page, and mail logs showed no clicks or replies.
